title: Policy routing adaptor and fallback simulation harness
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Background: Our current routing rules config is a loosely validated DSL that encodes region affinity, capacity tiers, and fallback model variants. Accumulated ad-hoc extensions have created ambiguous behavior during rollouts and made safe schema migrations difficult. Purpose: Build a non-destructive policy routing adaptor plus a simulation harness that can (1) perform staged, backward-compatible upgrades of rule configs, (2) run large-scale simulated traffic against candidate rule changes, and (3) catch silent contract breaks (region mismatch, tier shadowing, lost fallbacks) before they reach production. Scope: - Introduce a shallow adaptor layer that can accept legacy rule documents and emit a canonical routing contract representation used by the runtime. The adaptor must preserve semantics but annotate ambiguities for manual review. - Provide a deterministic simulation harness that replays sampled traffic patterns (latency/region/tenant weight distributions) and reports divergences between current and candidate-routing outcomes. - Add config-level semantic checks (e.g., unreachable tiers, overlapping regional scopes, incompatible fallback chains) and clear diagnostic messages for operators. Non-goals: This ticket does not implement full runtime rollout orchestration or automated in-prod migrations; that will be follow-up work.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptor accepts existing DSL variants and outputs canonical routing contract (proof of concept on 3 legacy samples).
Simulation harness runs a 24h sampled traffic replay and produces per-tenant divergence reports with >= 95% determinism between runs.

Semantic checks detect at least 5 classes of common misconfigurations (regional overlap, dangling fallback, tier shadowing, weight sum inconsistency, missing model variant for fallback) and map each to actionable remediation steps.

Performance: adaptor + checks add <6ms median overhead to request path when run in validation-only mode, and simulation runs complete at 10k rps-equivalent within 2 hours on CI sizing used by runtime team.
Design doc + migration plan reviewed by runtime, product, and security; PR opened and passes unit/integration tests and a canary on staging routing tier.
description_notes: Design trade-offs: - Keep adaptor intentionally conservative: prefer surfacing potential semantic ambiguity rather than guessing aggressive rewrites. - Use an intermediate canonical contract that is simple (region sets, ordered tier list, explicit fallback chains) to reduce coupling to runtime internals. - Simulation-based verification chosen over heavy static typing because many routing outcomes depend on traffic distributions and runtime capacity policies. Technical approach: 1) Implement a modular adaptor with phased passes: parsing (loose), normalizing (resolves synonyms, expands region aliases), annotation (tags ambiguities), and emit (canonical JSON contract). 2) Build a deterministic simulator that consumes canonical contracts + traffic model + capacity hints and outputs routing traces and aggregated divergence metrics. 3) Integrate a semantic-check ruleset DSL (rule files in repo) that is extensible by SRE/product. 4) Add CI jobs: quick-sanity on PRs, full-simulation nightly. Migration plan: - Stage 1 (spike): run adaptor against historical configs, create ambiguity reports. - Stage 2 (canary): enable validation-only adaptor in staging; block config commits with high-severity findings. - Stage 3 (rollout): enable adaptor as a pre-processor in controlled clusters with manual approval gates. Rollback: keep ability to bypass adaptor with a deprecated-legacy flag for emergency.
